The Diyo Sea Code

We would rather miss a close photo than chase a dolphin.

“Responsible” only means something if it changes how the boat is operated. This is the clearest way to make Diyo different from standard Lovina offers.

1. No aggressive chasingIf dolphins move away, that behaviour is respected.
2. No feeding and no touchingWild animals stay wild. The trip is observation, not interference.
3. No fake promisesNo “guaranteed close encounter” and no guaranteed catch.
4. Private, calm, directThe trip feels like going out with a real local captain — not joining a tour conveyor belt.

FAQ

Straight answers before people ask on WhatsApp.

Can you guarantee Mahi Mahi?

No. Mahi Mahi are wild fish. Season, weather, current, sea conditions and luck all matter.

Do you chase the dolphins?

No. Diyo aims to observe dolphins respectfully and avoids aggressive chasing or forcing close encounters. The dolphins decide the distance.

Is the trip private?

Yes, the trips are positioned as private boat trips for your own small group, up to 4 guests.

What happens if the weather is bad?

Safety comes first. If sea conditions are not suitable, Diyo will discuss another time or date with you.

Can children join?

Usually yes, depending on age, sea conditions and available safety equipment. Please ask before booking.

Where do we meet?

Diyo confirms the exact Lovina meeting point directly on WhatsApp before the trip.

How do I book?

Send Diyo a WhatsApp message with your preferred date, number of guests and the tour you want.
